record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and listed result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a refusal probe on stock and already-abliterated models, testing refusal behavior with a different probe rather than reproducing the original direction-finding and ablation method.
record.gate_note: The README reports 0/10 refusals for both models on 10 benign-but-commonly-refused prompts and explicitly calls this a floor effect that cannot detect abliteration. It does not report a harmful-request compliance test. Throughput and prefill results do not measure refusal or general capability, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: This is a deployment and benchmark recipe that runs an already-abliterated checkpoint (huihui-ai, quantized by root4k) as a tool. Its only refusal measure is a 10-prompt benign over-refusal probe. Both stock and abliterated models scored 0/10, and the README itself calls this a floor effect: 'Not evidence either way.' No harmful-request refusal or compliance rate is reported for either model, so nothing bears on whether abliteration removes refusal. Everything else reported is throughput, prefill, concurrency and numeric parity of the inference engine.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong. The README does present the throughput parity as a quality claim. It states 'at zero quality cost from the abliteration' and 'The abliteration costs nothing', based only on decode tok/s (71.0 vs 71.0 code-edit, 53.0 vs 55.2 prose). It separately concedes that the 10-prompt over-refusal probe (0/10 for both models) has a floor effect and cannot detect the abliteration.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an already-abliterated, quantized checkpoint; the README does not describe finding or ablating a residual-stream direction. This is a recipe/tool repository, credited as a copy of drowzeys' recipe repository.
record.problems: The refusal probe contains only 10 benign prompts and is explicitly described as having a floor effect. No harmful-request compliance results are reported, and the README does not measure general capability.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included: the reported throughput, prefill, concurrency, and numerical parity measures do not report refusal behavior or general capability.

untested.parts: All parts: direction extraction, ablation, addition, and retained capability.
Whether the abliterated weights remove refusal on harmful requests. Whether capability is kept: only decode throughput was compared, not task quality.
All parts. The model has thinking on by default, but no refusal analysis is done on it.

missing.what: The repository lists scripts/eval_ab.py and refusal_probe.py, plus A/B result files, which were not read. Only the README's summary of the refusal probe is available. Any quality or capability A/B between stock and abliterated models in these files is unreported in the README.

record.verdict_notes: The 'zero quality cost' claim rests on speed metrics, not on output quality or capability benchmarks, so it cannot count as a capability-retention test for V2. The 52% MMLU figure is a truncation artefact of thinking mode, not tied to abliteration. The measurements are credited to a different author (drowzeys); this repository is a republished copy.

relation.reason: The study uses an abliterated model as its subject and reports only throughput, prefill, concurrency and numerics for its recipe. Its one refusal measure is explicitly non-diagnostic.

tranche.reason: This is a deployment and benchmark recipe that runs an abliterated checkpoint someone else released (huihui-ai's, quantized by root4k) as a tool. It does not describe finding or ablating a direction. Its only refusal measure is a benign over-refusal probe at floor (0/10 both). The stock-vs-abliterated 'parity' is decode throughput, not refusal or capability. Its results do not bear on whether any version holds, so the reader's earlier T2 call is rightly overruled.

source_check.notes: The text is the README only. refusal_probe.py and the raw results/*.json files are listed but not included, so the probe prompts and judge are unknown. All measurements are credited to drowzeys, not the repo owner. The authors_conclusion paraphrase is accurate: 'zero quality cost' and 'costs nothing' rest on decode tok/s parity (71.0 vs 71.0 code-edit, 53.0 vs 55.2 prose). The MMLU 52% figure is a thinking-truncation artefact, not a stock-vs-abliterated comparison.

statements.correction: Over-refusal probe of 10 benign-but-commonly-refused prompts. 0/10 refusals for stock Qwen3.8-27B oQ4e (r1) and for root4k/Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated-oQ4e-mtp (r2). The README calls this a floor effect that cannot detect the abliteration. No harmful-prompt refusal rate is reported. Study is T4 / uses_without_test with no V2 verdict. At most it is an untested or cannot_determine example, not limits_scope evidence; cite r1 and r2.
statements.problem: 0/10 for both models on benign prompts is right. But the statement files this study as limits_scope evidence on V2. The study is T4 with no verdict. Its only refusal measure is a benign over-refusal probe that the README calls a floor effect and 'Not evidence either way'. It measures no refusal of harmful requests, so it does not qualify V2. Under the rules, untested parts are never limits_scope. The statement also cites no rows, though r1 and r2 hold these values.
